prompt: coreutils chroot newroot identical old root directory behavior
answer:
When `NEWROOT` is identical to the existing `/`, GNU Coreutils `chroot` avoids making the `chroot` system call. This is done for consistency with systems where an unprivileged user may use `chroot` in this case.

It still changes the working directory to `/` by default. Use `--skip-chdir` to retain the existing working directory; that option is permitted only when `NEWROOT` is the old `/` directory.
